name: lead-quality-stands-out
about: LQ3c: an ordinary day whose lead-quality rows show many wrong numbers on one campaign and many missed hard requirements on the other — the part the office most needs.

output.headline: November 3, 2026: 2 campaigns spent $284.25, delivered 7 leads at $40.61 each across 14,600 impressions and 203 clicks.
points: Regional Class A — Joliet led the day: $184.50 spent, 9,120 impressions, 141 clicks at 1.5%, 6 leads at $30.75 each. Dedicated night runs spent $99.75 for 1 lead at $99.75, with 62 clicks at 1.1% from 5,480 impressions.
Month to date in November 2026, Meta has taken $612.30 of spend with 28 days left in the month.

Lead quality over the last 14 days: Regional Class A — Joliet had 7 wrong numbers out of 15 called — a wrong-number share of 46.7% — which stands out and is worth a look at how those leads are sourced. 3 of its 24 leads missed a hard requirement (12.5% of leads). Median time to first call was 11 minutes.

Lead quality over the last 14 days: Dedicated night runs had 5 of its 9 leads miss a hard requirement — 55.6% of leads — which is high and worth attention. Wrong numbers were 1 of 8 called (12.5%). Median time to first call was 42 minutes, notably slower than the other campaign.

The 2026-09-21 cohort (38 leads) had 33 contacted, 17 made applicants, 10 applied, 4 hired, and 8 lost after conversion. The 2026-09-28 cohort (40 leads) had 36 contacted, 20 made applicants, 12 applied, 5 hired, and 9 lost after conversion.
The 2026-10-26 cohort has 12 leads — 9 contacted, 3 made applicants, 1 applied, and 1 lost after conversion — but it is too young to judge rates.
